subject: Day 28: schedule the 1-month visit
bodyText:
Today's focus
Avi is 28 days old and entering week 5, near the peak of the PURPLE crying curve. The action item is closing out the 1-month well check; inconsolable evenings this week are expected, not pathological.

Action items
- Schedule the 1-month well visit today if it is not already booked, and bring a feeding and output log so the pediatrician can plot growth on the WHO curves. AAP periodicity schedule: https://www.aap.org/en/practice-management/care-delivery-approaches/periodicity-schedule/
- Pre-schedule the 2-month visit for the day 56-70 window now; that round delivers HepB #2, RV #1, DTaP #1, Hib #1, PCV #1, and IPV #1. AAP immunization policy: https://www.aap.org/en/patient-care/immunizations/aap-policy-on-immunizations/
- Keep daycare tours and nanny interviews active this week if Anoushka or Noah is returning to work in the next 7-11 weeks.

Watch-fors
- [low concern] Inconsolable evening crying with no clear trigger is classic PURPLE crying; the 5 S's of swaddle, side or stomach hold, shush, swing, and suck help most infants settle.
- [monitor] Bloody or mucus-streaked stool can suggest milk-protein intolerance or an anal fissure; document it and let the pediatrician distinguish the two.
- [call within 24h] Sustained refusal of multiple feeds in a row warrants a same-day call.
- [call now] A rectal temperature of 100.4F or higher, apnea or color change, or inconsolable high-pitched crying with lethargy and a bulging fontanelle is an emergency; call the pediatrician or 911 now!

Enrichment opportunities
- Lean in close, brighten your whole face, and reward any flicker of a smile with obvious delight; consolidating social smiles is the week-5 social milestone. AAP Bright Futures: https://www.aap.org/en/practice-management/bright-futures/bright-futures-tools-and-resources/
- Read the same 3-5 board books on rotation rather than constantly new titles; the repetition is what lets rhythm and predictability start to register. AAP early literacy: https://www.aap.org/en/patient-care/early-childhood/early-literacy/
- Keep tummy time at 20-30 minutes cumulative across short bouts, using the forearm football hold for variety when floor time draws protest. AAP tummy time: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/sleep/Pages/Back-to-Sleep-Tummy-to-Play.aspx

Upcoming
- Day 28-35: 1-month well visit; bring the feeding and output log
- Day 35-41: Anoushka's 6-week postpartum OB visit; expect exercise clearance, contraception, and an EPDS screen
- Day 56-70: 2-month well visit; vaccines HepB #2, RV #1, DTaP #1, Hib #1, PCV #1, IPV #1

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- First social smile (responding to a face, not gas)
  AAP window: day 28-60
  What to look for: Smile in response to someone smiling or talking to them, not a reflexive gas smile. Hallmark social milestone.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/first-social-smile/complete

- Follows a moving object with eyes past midline
  AAP window: day 28-60
  What to look for: Hold a small object 8-12 inches away and slowly move side to side. Eyes should cross the body midline.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/tracks-moving-object/complete

- Seems happy to see you when you walk up
  AAP window: day 28-60
  What to look for: Recognition + positive affect. Often accompanied by limb-pumping excitement.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/seems-happy-to-see-you/complete

- Looks at a toy for several seconds
  AAP window: day 35-60 (coming up)
  What to look for: Sustained visual attention — precedes reaching.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/looks-at-toy-several-seconds/complete

- Coos or makes sounds beyond crying
  AAP window: day 35-60 (coming up)
  What to look for: Vowel sounds like ooh, ahh. Pre-language vocalization. Distinct from fussing or hiccup sounds.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/coos-makes-sounds/complete
